# Deep learning in plain English

::: {.partintro}
Part I's models were handed neat clues, like a threat-intel score. The real world hands you pixels, words and messy logs.

These four chapters show how models learn their own clues. We start from a single artificial neuron, then turn words into points in space, watch attention decide what to look at, and see what happens when all of it is trained at enormous scale.

Along the way we'll find out why the biggest models tend to be the most overconfident.
:::
